items.title: Vancomycin and zinc: starvation, assembly and resistance
items.content_text: Vancomycin can bind zinc, yet added zinc can also strengthen its activity in resistant bacteria. The experiments distinguish starvation from drug assembly.

items.title: Transferrin, ferritin and the race to recycle heme
items.content_text: How transferrin, ferritin, haptoglobin and hemopexin route iron, protect tissue and face microbial piracy—and which experiments distinguish those effects.

items.title: Silymarin, metal binding and the liver
items.content_text: Milk-thistle chemistry can bind or reduce metals, but nickel protection, lead measurements and human liver trials answer different mechanistic questions.

items.title: Parkinson’s dementia: shared copper depletion, distinct metal patterns
items.content_text: Brain copper loss in Parkinson’s dementia overlaps Alzheimer’s but differs by region. What this signature enables for microbial metallomics research.

items.title: Lactoferrin: iron withholding and microbial countermeasures
items.content_text: How lactoferrin withholds iron, disrupts microbial behavior, and faces bacterial countermeasures—and what oral human studies actually establish.

items.title: Hepcidin and ferroportin: iron redistribution in host defense
items.content_text: How hepcidin controls ferroportin, redistributes iron during inflammation, and creates different tradeoffs for microbes and red-cell production.

items.title: Glutathione, metals and the mitochondrial reserve
items.content_text: How glutathione supports enzymes, binds metals and enters mitochondria—and what drug metabolism does and does not establish about shared cellular reserve.

items.title: Endometriosis: do the metal and microbial signatures converge?
items.content_text: Trace iron retention, nickel, microbial signatures, nutritional immunity, and intervention evidence in endometriosis. A sourced test of competing mechanisms.

items.title: Dementia’s regional metal signatures
items.content_text: Dementia brain-metal signatures reveal regional copper loss and iron gain. A critical review connects these patterns to testable microbial-metallomics research.

items.title: Can probiotic yeast carry metals out of the gut?
items.content_text: How Saccharomyces boulardii and other yeasts bind lead, arsenic and mercury—and which experiments can distinguish adsorption from lasting removal.

items.title: Bile, metal export and the route back
items.content_text: Bile carries metal-containing cargo, but bile acids, glutathione complexes, copper pumps and microbial transformations govern different steps toward elimination.

items.title: Alzheimer’s disease: copper depletion and regional metal contrasts
items.content_text: Alzheimer’s brain copper loss and regional iron and zinc changes reveal a spatial disease signature—and define experiments for microbial metallomics.

items.title: Tampon Metals and the Vaginal Microbiome: The Blind Spot in the Risk Assessment
items.content_text: A 2026 FDA risk assessment by Jin et al. calls the metals in tampons safe, but only for one endpoint: the fraction absorbed systemically into the blood. That verdict rests on a single word, bioavailable. The vaginal microbes live on the surface, not in the bloodstream, and were never assessed.

items.title: Iron Fortification and the Kenyan Infant Gut Microbiome
items.content_text: A full review of Jaeggi et al. (Gut 2015): iron-fortified porridge increased pathogenic E. coli and enterobacteria, cut bifidobacteria, and inflamed the gut in Kenyan infants.

items.title: The Metal–Microbiome–Disease Axis: Who Gets the Metal?
items.content_text: Metals change microbial ecology; microbes change metal chemistry; inflammation changes local metal access. Follow the mechanisms connecting exposure, nutritional immunity, and disease.

items.title: Metals, the Microbiome, and Parkinson's: A Gut-First Pathway to Neurodegeneration
items.content_text: How heavy-metal exposure may reshape the gut microbiome and feed gut-first alpha-synuclein pathology in Parkinson's disease - a metallomic-microbiome view.

items.title: Mercury, Methylmercury, and the Microbiome: How Gut Microbes Shape Neurotoxic Risk
items.content_text: How gut microbes methylate and demethylate mercury via hgcAB and merB, how mercury reshapes the microbiome, and why this shapes methylmercury neurotoxic risk.

items.title: How Low-Dose Heavy Metals May Reshape the Gut Microbiome to Drive Obesity
items.content_text: Low-dose arsenic, cadmium, and lead may reshape the gut microbiome, depleting SCFA producers and promoting obesity and metabolic syndrome. Evidence examined.

items.title: How Dietary Nickel Arms Gut Bacteria — and May Fuel Gut Disease
items.content_text: Dietary nickel activates nickel-dependent virulence enzymes in gut Enterobacteriaceae — a mechanistic pathway that may link nickel exposure to NEC and IBD.

items.title: Feeding the Enemy: How Dietary Iron Reshapes the Gut Microbiome and Raises Enteric Infection Risk
items.content_text: Unabsorbed iron can alter the gut microbiome and intestinal inflammation. Human trials show that effects on diarrhea vary by setting and formulation.

items.title: Does Lead Harm the Developing Brain Through the Gut Microbiome?
items.content_text: Animal and human cohort studies link lead exposure to gut microbiome dysbiosis, a candidate mediator of lead's neurodevelopmental harm via the gut-brain axis.

items.title: Cadmium and the Gut Microbiome: A Hidden Route to Metabolic Disease
items.content_text: Cadmium reshapes the gut microbiome, depletes Lachnospiraceae, weakens the gut barrier, and is linked to hepatic and metabolic dysfunction. An evidence review.

items.title: Arsenic and the Gut Microbiome: A Two-Way Street
items.content_text: Arsenic reshapes the gut microbiome, and gut bacteria shape arsenic's toxicity in return. See the bidirectional evidence linking metals, microbes, and disease.

items.title: Six Decades of Fertilizer Use Built a Legacy of Cadmium, Nickel, and Lead in Soils and Diets
items.content_text: Preprint — A food metallomics review (1960–2025) showing how phosphate and urea fertilizers loaded soils, crops, and diets with cadmium, nickel, lead, and chromium.

items.title: Heavy Metals and Microbial Metallomics: A New Framework for the US Obesity Epidemic
items.content_text: Preprint — How dietary cadmium, arsenic, lead, and nickel may disrupt gut microbial metallomics—driving dysbiosis, inflammation, and insulin resistance behind obesity.

items.title: Developmental Readiness Is Not Toxicokinetic Safety: Heavy Metals in Vegetable-Based Baby Foods
items.content_text: Preprint — Developmental readiness for solids does not ensure toxicokinetic safety: leafy greens, brassicas and root crops concentrate lead, cadmium and arsenic in baby foods.

items.title: Concentration-Based Heavy Metal Standards to Reduce Real Exposure in Infant and Child Foods
items.content_text: Standard — HMTc 2026 sets concentration-based, as-sold action levels for lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury, nickel and other heavy metals in infant and child foods.

items.title: Nickel as a Catalytic Driver of Necrotizing Enterocolitis
items.content_text: Journal article — Dietary nickel in infant formula may activate nickel-dependent microbial enzymes (urease, glyoxalase I) that drive necrotizing enterocolitis in preterm infants.

items.title: A Unified Model for FIP-Associated Gingivitis in Cats: Disrupting Microbial Shielding and Restoring Nutritional Immunity
items.content_text: Journal article — How itraconazole and lactoferrin may treat FIP-linked gingivitis in cats by disrupting polymicrobial biofilms and restoring metal-based nutritional immunity.

items.title: Microbiome Medicine Journal: Restoring Causal Structure to Disease Through Microbial Metallomics
items.content_text: Journal — Microbiome Medicine Journal Vol. I sets out a mechanism-first framework linking microbial ecology, host metallome regulation, and metal dyshomeostasis to disease.

items.title: From Dysbiosis to Dyshomeostasis: Reframing Parkinson's Through a Metallomic–Microbiome Lens
items.content_text: Journal article — A metallomics framework reframes Parkinson's as metal dyshomeostasis: iron, manganese, copper, zinc and nickel dysregulation drives dysbiosis and neuron loss.

items.title: The MC1R–Parkinson's Link May Be a Metallomic Story, Not a Cosmetic One
items.content_text: Journal article — A hypothesis linking MC1R red-hair variants to Parkinson's risk via melanin-metal chemistry: how copper, zinc, and iron shape neuromelanin's redox buffering.

items.title: Parkinson's Disease as a Disorder of Metal Dyshomeostasis Amplified by Microbial Ecology
items.content_text: Journal article — A synthesis framework proposing Parkinson's disease begins with heavy-metal dyshomeostasis that drives ferroptosis, gut dysbiosis, and α-synuclein pathology.

items.title: Prenatal Tobacco Exposure and the Child Gut Microbiome
items.content_text: Prenatal smoking and childhood gut taxa were associated in an observational cohort; the responsible exposure components remain unresolved.

items.title: Prenatal Metal Exposure, the Gut Microbiome, and Childhood Intestinal Inflammation
items.content_text: A 2024 PROGRESS cohort study links prenatal copper and cesium exposure, interacting with specific gut microbes, to elevated fecal calprotectin in children.

items.title: Prenatal Acetaminophen, the Infant Gut Microbiome, and Childhood Cognition
items.content_text: GESTE cohort links prenatal acetaminophen and caffeine to childhood gut microbiome shifts and cognition; Proteobacteria abundance modified WISC-IV scores.

items.title: Pediatric Gut Microbiome Composition in Health: What a Systematic Review Reveals
items.content_text: A systematic review of 42 studies finds geography, diet, and 16S sequencing method, not age, shape healthy children's Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes gut profiles.

items.title: Lactoferrin vs. Ferrous Sulfate Through a Metallomics Lens
items.content_text: Meta-analyses show oral lactoferrin can match or outperform ferrous sulfate for iron repletion, lowering IL-6 and hepcidin with fewer gut side effects.

items.title: Lactobacillus plantarum 299v and Oral Iron Therapy Tolerance
items.content_text: A randomized trial shows the probiotic Lactobacillus plantarum 299v reduces oral iron side effects and improves iron status in iron-deficiency anemia patients.

items.title: Iron- and Zinc-Biofortified Foods and the Gut Microbiota
items.content_text: Systematic review of iron/zinc-biofortified bean and wheat diets in the Gallus gallus model: staples raised SCFA-producing Lactobacillus and cut enteric pathogens.

items.title: Iron Supplements and the Gut Microbiome in Reproductive-Age Women: A Randomized Controlled Trial
items.content_text: A 21-day randomized placebo-controlled trial found ferrous fumarate did not significantly alter fecal microbiome composition in Australian reproductive-age women.

items.title: Iron Fortification, the Infant Gut Microbiome, and Diarrhea Risk
items.content_text: Iron fortification shifts the infant gut microbiome toward enterobacteria and pathogenic E. coli, cutting protective bifidobacteria and raising diarrhea risk.

items.title: Intestinal Biomarkers and the Non-Motor Phenotype of Parkinson's Disease
items.content_text: Parkinson's patients with constipation show higher fecal calprotectin, reduced SCFAs, lower gut diversity, and greater IBD genetic risk, linking gut inflammation to non-motor severity.

items.title: HERFD-XAS: High-Resolution X-ray Speciation of Biological Metals
items.content_text: HERFD-XAS sharpens X-ray absorption spectra by rejecting core-hole broadening, resolving mercury, selenium, and arsenic speciation in dilute biological samples for metallomics.

items.title: Gut Microbiome and Childhood Stunting in Low- and Middle-Income Countries
items.content_text: Systematic review of 14 studies links childhood stunting in LMICs to inflammatory gut pathobionts and depleted butyrate producers, driving impaired linear growth.

items.title: Childhood Blood Metals and the Gut Microbiome: Evidence from the GESTE Cohort
items.content_text: GESTE cohort links childhood blood metals (Mn, Se, Cd, Hg, Pb) to gut microbiome composition in 6-7 year olds; manganese and selenium tied to bacterial phyla.

items.title: A Multi-Omics + MR Enterography Model for Predicting Bowel Damage in Crohn's Disease
items.content_text: Two-center study fusing gut microbiome, fecal and serum metabolomics, and MR enterography into a model predicting cumulative Crohn's bowel damage (AUC 0.857).

items.title: The Human Microbiome Across Body Sites: Gut, Skin, Oral, Vaginal and Lung
items.content_text: How the human microbiome differs across the gut, skin, oral, vaginal and lung niches, how it is acquired and disrupted, and why heavy-metal exposure matters.

items.title: Prenatal Metal Exposure, the Gut Microbiome, and Childhood Depression
items.content_text: A Mexico City birth-cohort study links a prenatal zinc-cobalt profile plus specific gut bacteria to 15.4% higher childhood depression scores at ages 9-11.

items.title: Prenatal Lead Exposure and the Childhood Gut Microbiome
items.content_text: Prenatal lead exposure is negatively linked to the childhood gut microbiome: metagenomics from a Mexico City cohort ties maternal Pb to fewer beneficial bacteria.

items.title: Prebiotics Blunt the Gut Cost of Iron-Fortified Cereal in Kenyan Infants
items.content_text: In a Kenyan infant RCT, adding prebiotic GOS/FOS to iron-fortified cereal raised iron absorption 60% and reduced gut inflammation, pathogens, and dysbiosis.

items.title: Nutritional Immunity and Trace Metals in Infection
items.content_text: How the host uses iron, zinc, manganese and copper handling as nutritional immunity to starve or poison pathogens, plus metal-based therapeutic strategies.

items.title: Metal Availability and Immune Function During Infection
items.content_text: How zinc, iron, manganese, and copper availability shapes neutrophil and macrophage function during infection through nutritional immunity, calprotectin, and phagosomal metal handling.

items.title: Iron Chelation Therapy in Transfusion-Dependent Thalassemia
items.content_text: Clinical review of deferoxamine, deferiprone, and deferasirox for transfusion iron overload in thalassemia, covering cardiac and hepatic iron outcomes measured by MRI T2*.

items.title: Heavy Metals and the Gut Microbiota: A Systematic Review
items.content_text: Systematic review of 12 human studies links arsenic, lead, mercury, and cadmium exposure to gut microbiota dysbiosis, leaky gut, and disease, with dietary mitigation.

items.title: Gallium as an Iron Mimic: Disrupting Pseudomonas Iron Metabolism in Cystic Fibrosis
items.content_text: Gallium substitutes for iron to sabotage Pseudomonas aeruginosa iron metabolism. A Phase 1 CF trial (Goss et al., Sci Transl Med 2018) found IV gallium improved lung function.

items.title: Copper in Infectious Disease: Both Sides of the Penny
items.content_text: How the immune system weaponizes copper against pathogens: macrophage copper bursts, phagosomal intoxication, fungal copper detox, and copper nutritional immunity.

items.title: Arsenic Exposure Reshapes the Gut Microbiome of Bangladeshi Children, Enriching Resistance-Carrying E. coli
items.content_text: Arsenic-exposed Bangladeshi children carry more gut Proteobacteria and E. coli bearing arsenic-resistance (ars) and antibiotic-resistance-like genes, a metal-microbiome case study.

items.title: Proteome-Scale Mapping of Iron-Binding Proteins in Bread Wheat
items.content_text: A proteome-wide scan of bread wheat mapped ~600 iron-binding proteins with Fe(II)/Fe(III) sites coordinated by His, Glu, Asp and Cys, aiding metallomics.

items.title: Colorectal cancer: mapping metals, cells, and microbial questions
items.content_text: Colorectal cancer metal maps reveal distinct copper and iron neighborhoods. What they measured, and how to test microbial access, host response and disease.

items.title: [NiFe]-Hydrogenase Cofactor Biosynthesis and the Hyp Maturation Proteins (HypA-F) in E. coli
items.content_text: How E. coli builds the NiFe(CN)2CO cofactor of [NiFe]-hydrogenases: the HypA-F maturation proteins, cyanide and CO ligand synthesis, and nickel insertion.

items.title: The Zinc Clasp: How Zn2+ Shapes T-Cell Signaling
items.content_text: The zinc clasp is a Zn2+-bridged interface that tethers the kinase Lck to CD4 and CD8 coreceptors, a labile-zinc switch central to T-cell activation and immunity.

items.title: The Iron Metalloproteome of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Under Oxic and Anoxic Conditions
items.content_text: Native metalloproteomics maps how Pseudomonas aeruginosa partitions iron across four protein complexes, with denitrification raising iron demand in anoxia.

items.title: Nitric Oxide Sensing by the [4Fe-4S] Regulator ArnR
items.content_text: ArnR uses a [4Fe-4S] cluster to sense nitric oxide: NO nitrosylates the cluster, abolishing DNA binding and derepressing nitrate-respiration and hmp genes.

items.title: Maternal metallomics: what UPBEAT opens for microbial research
items.content_text: UPBEAT links maternal manganese and phosphorus to later outcomes. What the evidence means, and how to test host and microbial metal handling.

items.title: Iron-Sulfur Clusters and Oxygen in Human Disease
items.content_text: How iron-sulfur (Fe-S) cluster biogenesis and oxygen shape human disease: NFS1 in lung cancer, hyperoxia injury, and hypoxia therapy for Friedreich ataxia.
